image: A supply and demand graph for labour, with 'wage ($)' on the y-axis and 'labour (millions)' on the x-axis. Initial demand (D₁D₁) and supply (S₁S₁) curves intersect at an equilibrium. Question_text: By 2014, government subsidies for the Chinese steel industry led to 200 million tonnes of excess output. The diagrams show the market for Chinese steel. Which would represent the position after the subsidy but before the market adjusted?
image: Four supply and demand graphs (A, B, C, D) for the market for Chinese steel. Each graph shows price ($) on the y-axis and output (million tonnes) on the x-axis. Option A shows an initial equilibrium, then a rightward shift of the supply curve (S to S') leading to a lower price and higher quantity supplied. Option B shows a similar rightward shift of supply, but also indicates an excess supply at the original price. Option C shows a rightward shift of the supply curve. Option D shows an initial equilibrium and a rightward shift in the demand curve. The key is to identify the graph that represents an increase in supply due to a subsidy, resulting in excess output before the price adjusts to a new equilibrium.
